subject: MediWell evaluation: acceptance tests, evidence, and owner assignments
messages:
From: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@mediwell.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediWell Procurement <procurement@mediwell.com>
Date: 2027-03-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Defining acceptance evidence for MediWell evaluation

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at MediWell is excited to continue. Procurement asked me to capture a concise list of what Redwood will need to deliver (and what we'll need to provide) to consider the evaluation a success. We want to make sure there are no surprises at contract close.

Can you please:
- Confirm the acceptance tests you expect to run during the 2-week pilot smoke window
- List the exact observability artifacts (logs, per-route latency SLO reports, token cost samples) we must see as evidence
- Assign an internal owner for each acceptance test (so we know who to ping)

If you can share a short checklist or spreadsheet with owners and pass/fail thresholds that would be ideal. We hope to finalize the MAP and sign the mutual commitments by the end of next week.

Claire Zhang
Senior PM, Evaluation Programs
MediWell

--
Attachment: procurement-questions.pdf (stub)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@mediwell.com>
Date: 2027-03-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Defining acceptance evidence for MediWell evaluation

Claire — thanks, clear ask. I'm looping in the owners and attaching a first-pass checklist. High level below, and I'll update the shared doc with explicit owners and links.

Draft acceptance checklist (summary):
1) Functional correctness (sample dataset pass rate)
   - Test: 500 representative prompts from MediWell test suite, >= 92% pass on core intent/slot extraction
   - Evidence: CSV of inputs/outputs + concordance score; owner: Marissa Cole

2) Latency & tail behavior
   - Test: 95th percentile latency under pilot traffic <= 350ms for 512-token sequences
   - Evidence: per-route P95/P99 traces and sample Request-IDs; owner: Ben Carter

3) Cost and throughput validation
   - Test: sustained throughput target (X rps) with unit cost samples within 10% of forecast
   - Evidence: token-level cost report for representative hour; owner: Dylan Brooks

4) Observability & instrumentation
   - Test: dashboards and alerting hooks confirmed (logs, traces, token-cost sampling, anomaly alerts)
   - Evidence: read-only links + screenshots; owner: Grace O'Connor

I attached \"MW-eval-acceptance-checklist.xlsx\" with details and draft pass/fail cells. Next steps: owners confirm thresholds and we lock dates.

Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: MW-eval-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (stub)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@mediwell.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Defining acceptance evidence for MediWell evaluation

Thanks for the draft, Dylan — a few concrete adjustments from the observability/ops side so the evidence is unambiguous for MediWell's reviewers:

Operational acceptance additions:
- Sampling window: require 3 non-consecutive 1-hour windows during pilot with telemetry captured (not just a single sample hour). Helps catch burst behavior.
- KV-cache priming: call out that prefix-caching validation requires a separate test vector; pass condition is >= 5% latency improvement on repeated requests for the same session footprint.
- Failure mode proof: provide induced-error run (short 10m simulated gpu OOMs fallback) to show graceful degradation and fallback policy kicks in. Evidence = annotated trace + fallback metrics.
- Log retention sample: provide a 7-day export sample subset for audit.

Owners (proposal):
- Observability artifacts & dashboards: Grace O'Connor (owner)
- Instrumentation checklist & runbooks: Ben Carter (owner)
- Functional concordance and test vectors: Marissa Cole (owner)

I'll drop a small markdown doc with the observability hooks — attaching here. Also proposing we add a column in the spreadsheet for \"evidence link\" so MediWell can validate directly.

Grace
VP, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: observability-hooks.md (stub)

Dylan / Grace — this is helpful, thank you. A few clarifying points from the MediWell side:

- For functional correctness we will provide the 500-item test vector by end of day Friday. We'll include a short list of high-priority intents we consider blocking.
- For latency/throughput, procurement asks that we also capture a 95th percentile during a simulated concurrent session pattern (we can provide the JMeter script).
- On observability: we need read-only dashboard links and one hour of raw logs for our security team to sample.
- Owners: Procurement will only accept named contact emails for legal signoff — please provide names + emails for the four owners in the checklist.

Can we lock the pilot smoke window to start Monday 2027-03-15, run for 10 business days, and then have a formal review call on 2027-03-29? If we hit all acceptance tests on 3/29 we'll proceed to a contract signature the following week.

Claire
Senior PM, Evaluation Programs
MediWell

- Security team has sampled logs and confirmed no high-severity concerns (they will email procurement with findings)

Deliverables we will share by 2027-03-12
- Finalized spreadsheet with owners + evidence links (Dylan)
- Observability hook doc and runbook (Grace)
- Test vector ingestion confirmation and JMeter script (MediWell)

Next steps for procurement/legal
- I will attach the MAP appendix to the MAA draft and add the dates above. Procurement, please confirm if you need any additional evidence types (SOC2 artifact extract, data deletion cadence, etc.) so we can include those in the MAP.

I'll push updates to the shared doc and mark cells with owner emails. If that looks good I'll open a quick 20m call Wednesday morning to walk through the runbook.

Thanks all — Dylan
